title: Mixed-cup NormalizedScalars
statement:
Fix an algebraically closed geometric point $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ with datum and coefficient stages as in [def-sf-mixed-cup-coefficient-passages]. Let $R\to T$ be a morphism of commutative ring sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $A\to B$ be a commutative ring map, and let $A\to\Gamma(s,R)$ and $B\to\Gamma(s,T)$ be bijective coefficient maps forming a square. Define the section functors by final-object evaluation and restriction of the coefficient action. The ordinary scalar/section comparison is the unique natural isomorphism sending $b\otimes x$ to the section $j(b)\otimes x$. For exact section functors its derived comparison is the unique natural isomorphism between ordinary derived coefficient extension after sections and sections after ringed derived extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], whose composite with the two universal derived counits on every flat-term K-flat representative is the localization of that ordinary balanced map. Existence and uniqueness are asserted for both comparisons, without flatness of the coefficient map.

Use the constant coefficient systems and their actual constant-section pullback maps at finite stages, and the completed integral coefficient system of [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data] at integral stages. The actual constant and completed section maps are bijective, and their squares commute for arbitrary finite-ring maps, integral reduction and completed integral extension; this defines the elementary ringed-passage point comparison. Constant coefficient pullback squares commute as well. Finally an exact ordinary coefficient extension has the unique comparison of its universal left-derived functor with its exact termwise derived functor whose equation is its universal counit on every complex. For fields the coefficient/carrier lift of [def-sf-point-fibre-tensor-rational-compatibility] commutes with scalar extension by the unique comparison which sends $b\otimes\mathrm{up}(x)$ to $\mathrm{up}(\mathrm{down}(b)\otimes x)$ and is derived by the specified localization factorizations. These specifications define the normalized scalar coordinates; no unspecified isomorphism is selected. The actual integral reduction and completed coefficient changes are those of [def-sp-coefficient-mate-comparisons].
